core_obligations: Write down the commutative square obtained from the adjunction identity, with vertical arrows that are isomorphisms (proof lines 1225-1233).
Forward direction: universal injectivity makes the rows surjective at the test object C(M), so the identity of C(M) lifts to a splitting of C(f) (proof lines 1234-1239).
Converse: a splitting makes the rows surjective for every P, and faithfulness of C turns that into injectivity of every base change of f (proof lines 1240-1242).
proof_roadmap: Forward direction by lifting the identity (proof lines 1234-1239).
difficulty_reason: For a ring R and a morphism f: M to N of modules, the lemma shows that f is universally injective exactly when the induced map C(N) to C(M) is a split surjection (statement lines 1218-1222). The proof uses the adjunction identity to replace the induced map on Hom groups by the base changed map inside C, exhibiting a commutative square whose vertical arrows are isomorphisms (proof lines 1224-1233). The forward direction then reads surjectivity of the rows at P equal to C(M), which lets the identity of C(M) be lifted to a splitting of C(f); the converse uses surjectivity of the rows for arbitrary P together with faithfulness of C to conclude that every base change of f is injective (proof lines 1234-1242). The claim is H2: a short but complete argument whose content is the correct choice of the test object P and the two one-line transfers.
